conventions.convention: The fine equation is F_h(u)=f_h. Iterate restriction I, residual restriction R, and prolongation P are independent linear maps. After pre-smoothing, the coarse target is F_H(Iu)+R(f_h−F_h(u)); tau is F_H(Iu)−RF_h(u), and correction is u+P(v−Iu).

Arithmetic is exact. Smoother counts and solver budgets are finite; exact-root means zero residual, while inexact-root means a positive explicitly computed residual. Final status certifies the returned iterate's own level equation.

Levels run from 0 to J, with 0 the base level. Each recursive call lowers the level; repeated coarse calls retain the same target and start from the latest coarse iterate. V and W use one and two calls respectively.
The exact coarse branch passes through Iu_* and has invertible DF_H(Iu_*); the pre/post smoothing maps fix u_*.

All derivative norms are induced Euclidean operator norms. The local theorem gives contraction of errors toward the fixed root with factor q+Lr/2, rather than asserting contraction between every pair of points.

Linear reduction assumes an SPD Galerkin hierarchy, full-column-rank prolongations, R_j=P_j transpose, matching residual-correction smoothers and cycle counts; I_j may be any linear map of the stated dimensions.
The coarse residual-to-solution estimate is an independent hypothesis; invertibility of the coarse Jacobian alone does not supply it.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the finite-budget two-grid procedure: pre-smooth, form g_H=F_H(Iu)+R(f_h−F_h(u)), make finitely many coarse calls, correct by P(z−Iu), post-smooth, and report the final fine residual and status.
Defines a finite hierarchy whose noncoarsest levels use the two-grid procedure with the next-level cycle as coarse solver, finite metered budgets, and one or two repeated coarse calls.

Under root-fixing smoothers, admissible restrictions selected as exact coarse roots at zero defect, and a base solver preserving initial exact roots, the exact-branch FAS V/W cycle leaves an exact fine root fixed, for arbitrary admissible transfers.
For the actual C1 exact-branch cycle fixing u_*, on a closed radius-r ball with q=‖DE(u_*)‖<1 and L-Lipschitz derivative, q+Lr/2<1 implies ball invariance and ‖u_k−u_*‖≤(q+Lr/2)^k‖u_0−u_*‖.
Under its C1, selected-branch, fixed-root and invertible-coarse-Jacobian hypotheses, DE(u_*)=DS_post(u_*)[Id−P DF_H(Iu_*)⁻¹ R DF_h(u_*)]DS_pre(u_*).
For compatible C2 maps E=T∘C∘S, the second derivative is D²T(z)[DC(y)DS(x)h,DC(y)DS(x)k]+DT(z)(D²C(y)[DS(x)h,DS(x)k]+DC(y)D²S(x)[h,k]), where y=S(x) and z=C(y).
For the linear Galerkin V/W procedure, Cycle(j,x+a,b+A_ja)=a+Cycle(j,x,b), with identical hierarchy, smoothing matrices, sweep counts and cycle count.

Under the stated SPD Galerkin hierarchy, transpose residual restriction, matching smoothers and finite cycle counts, exact-branch linear FAS returns exactly the corresponding Galerkin correction V/W iterate; iterate restriction may be any linear map of the stated dimensions.

published_dependencies.used_for: Completeness of the finite-dimensional vector and operator spaces used in the second-derivative composition lemma.
Chain and bounded-bilinear product rules when differentiating products of derivative operators.
Existence, C1 regularity and derivative formula for the selected coarse branch through Iu_*.
Differentiation of the actual pre-smoother, coarse-correction and post-smoother composition.
The quadratic Taylor remainder, with endpoints reversed to obtain the linear term DE(u_*).
Converting the examples' explicit second-derivative bounds into derivative-Lipschitz estimates on convex balls.
